name: Hall in Tirol
kurzbeschreibung: Historic old town featuring the famous Haller Münzturm and one of the best-preserved city centers in Tirol.
beschreibung:
Overview

Hall in Tirol is situated at an elevation of 574 metres in the Lower Inn Valley within the district of Innsbruck-Land, roughly ten kilometres east of the provincial capital Innsbruck. The historic town lies along the northern bank of the River Inn at the foot of the dramatic Karwendel mountains and counts around 14,500 residents. Hall boasts the largest preserved medieval Old Town in Western Austria, surpassing even Innsbruck in historical surface area. Winding cobblestone alleys, magnificent Gothic and Baroque patrician houses, and inviting town squares give Hall its unforgettable atmosphere. Once the economic powerhouse of Tyrol, the town today blends fascinating heritage with vibrant culture, fine dining, and welcoming alpine livability.

History

The origins and remarkable prosperity of Hall are deeply rooted in salt, once known as white gold. The town was first documented in 1256 as a salt manufacturing centre (salina in Valle). Rock salt extracted from the Halltal valley was boiled down in the saltworks and shipped downstream via the River Inn as far as Bavaria and Hungary. In 1303, Duke Otto of Carinthia-Tyrol granted Hall city rights. Hall achieved world renown from 1477 onwards, when Archduke Sigismund the Rich relocated the sovereign mint from Merano to Hall. Here, in 1486, the famous Guldiner was struck—the first high-denomination silver coin, which served as the precursor to the Taler and ultimately inspired the American dollar. In 1567, the mint moved into Hasegg Castle, whose towering Mint Tower remains the landmark of the city.

Getting There

Hall in Tirol enjoys ideal transportation links. By automobile, the city is quickly reached via the Inntal Motorway A12 using exits Hall-Mitte or Hall-West, as well as via the federal highway B171. Train travellers benefit from exceptional regional connections: Hall in Tirol railway station is served frequently by Tyrol S-Bahn lines S4 and S5 as well as Regional-Express services, connecting to Innsbruck Central Station in under ten minutes. Furthermore, frequent regional bus lines (including VVT routes 504 and 505) link Hall directly with downtown Innsbruck. Cyclists can pedal smoothly along the Inn Valley Cycle Path directly to the town gates.

Tips

A visit to medieval Hasegg Castle and the Hall Mint Museum (Museum Münze Hall) is essential; ascending the twelve-sided Mint Tower offers sweeping vistas over the tiled roofs and the Inn Valley. Strolling through the town reveals architectural masterworks such as the Upper Town Square, the Gothic Town Hall, and the monumental St. Nicholas Parish Church. Connoisseurs will delight in the weekly Hall Farmers' Market and the enchanting Christmas Market. Outdoor enthusiasts can venture directly into the Karwendel Nature Park, where the scenic Halltal valley offers historic hiking routes to old brine mining shafts and the secluded St. Magdalena hermitage.
